skills.name: Upjohn
skills.description: Properly identifies representation and role with the Company, and that they cannot give the employee legal advice. This must always be part of the very beginning of the interview.
skills.reason: T2 identifies the Committee and company as client, states 'not you personally', says counsel cannot give legal advice, at the very start.

skills.name: Privilege
skills.description: Properly explains that the Company controls the privilege and determines how it is shared.
skills.reason: T2 says the privilege belongs to the company and the company may decide to share what is said, including with the government.

skills.name: Relationship
skills.description: Establishes rapport and interview expectations. This includes: establishes an appropriate professional tone; explains how the interview will proceed; encourages complete answers; instructs the witness that they can speculate, they just need to say when they do; invites the witness to distinguish between recollection and uncertainty.
skills.reason: Professional tone only; no ground rules on speculation, estimates, or distinguishing recollection from uncertainty, and the interview process is not explained.

skills.name: Confirmation
skills.description: Checks the witness understood the Upjohn warning and answers their questions, if any.
skills.reason: T2 asks 'Any questions?' and T3 confirms understanding, but the witness's mention of own counsel in T3 is never addressed.

skills.name: Closing
skills.description: Closes by confirming there is "nothing else", next steps, a confidentiality reminder, and a reminder to keep records.
skills.reason: T150 asks if there is anything else; T158 gives a confidentiality reminder and a document-keeping instruction, but no next steps.

moments.text: We represent the Committee and the company, not you personally.
the company may decide to share what you tell us with others, including the government.

skills.name: Narrative Development
skills.description: Lets the witness walk through what happened.
skills.reason: Open prompts such as 'Tell me everything you remember' at T12, T24, T32 and T46 let the witness walk through events.

skills.name: Funneling
skills.description: Moves in a sensible order from general to specific questions.
skills.reason: Moves from role and reporting lines (T4-T9) to specific deals, though some topics jump between deals.

skills.name: Clarity
skills.description: Asks clear questions and avoids compound, ambiguous, or legalistic questions.
skills.reason: Most questions are short and clear; a few, such as T116, combine a document reference with a request to explain.

skills.name: Professionalism
skills.description: Stays neutral, polite and in control.
skills.reason: Remains polite and in control; questions such as T82 press the witness without being hostile.

skills.name: Adaptability
skills.description: Changes technique based on the witness's answers rather than staying only with the outline.
skills.reason: Moves from the Foundation question to the Southampton agreement (T69-T80) and to the Andy note after the witness's answers (T132-T136).

areas.name: Fact Development, Source Identification, & Credibility Testing

skills.name: Ensures Credibility
skills.description: Recognizes and follows up on incomplete, evasive, or inconsistent answers.
skills.reason: Evasions left unchallenged on key points: 'I don't recall it coming up' (T45), 'Some approvals were papered after' (T53), 'I don't believe it came up' (T93) and 'I may have said it should be resolved' (T149).

skills.name: Material Facts
skills.description: Identifies the who, what, when, and how.
skills.reason: Covers who negotiated the unwind, who managed Chewco, and when the Foundation invested, though some how and when details are left open.

skills.name: Memory Refreshing
skills.description: Tries other ways when the witness can't remember.
skills.reason: The interviewer used documents to refresh memory at T72, T98 and T132 and used the Southampton figures at T80, but did not show the Raptor I approval sheet when the witness said I would have to look at the sheet at T53.

skills.name: Establishes Knowledge
skills.description: Separates what the witness personally knows from speculation, secondhand information, or inferences.
skills.reason: Did not separate personal knowledge from hearsay on 'I believe he told the Board' (T41) or Kopper's handling of the payment (T139-T141).

skills.name: Other Sources
skills.description: Identifies additional witnesses.
skills.reason: T152 asks who else to speak with and the witness names Causey, Buy, Glisan, Kopper, Andersen and V&E.

skills.name: Other Evidence
skills.description: Identifies other documents such as communications, reports, notes, or other relevant records.
skills.reason: T154 asks about documents and T156 asks about personal notes and emails, which the witness then identifies.

skills.name: Tests Certainty
skills.description: Examines how certain the witness is about their memory or a fact.
skills.reason: Hedges such as 'I may have mentioned it' (T97), 'They may have put it that way' (T147) and 'Something modest' (T127) were not pressed on how certain the witness was.

skills.name: Follow-Up
skills.description: Recognizes material responses and follows up on them.
skills.reason: Most key leads were followed up, but at least seven key leads (T15, T17, T31, T53, T57, T149, T157) were never followed up, which caps the rating at 2.

moments.text: We represent the Committee and the company, not you personally. We're not your attorney and can't give you legal advice.
Witness said he understood the interviewer was not his lawyer and that he may want his own counsel later.
Is there anything I haven't asked about that you think the Committee should know?
Please keep any documents related to this, and don't discuss this interview with anyone.
Tell me everything you remember about how LJM1 came about in 1999.
Tell me everything you remember about how Chewco came to be formed in 1997.
Tell me everything you remember about the controls put in place when the Board approved LJM2 in October 1999.
Take a specific deal.

area_evidence.area: Fact Development, Source Identification, & Credibility Testing

moments.text: Asked who Glisan reported to; witness said to him, but that Glisan was 'perfectly capable' of representing Enron. The conflict was not pursued.
Approximately, then. Were they above or below the 30 percent the Board was shown?
In June 1999 you told the Board you would receive no value from the Enron stock in LJM. How does a $4.5 million return fit with that?
The Finance Committee materials show 17.95 percent. In October 2000, LJM2's limited partners were told the projected return was 51 percent. Help me understand the difference.
Confronted witness's denial of Chewco buyout involvement with the 'Andy' note; he answered that being informed is not negotiating.
Witness said he did not recall Kopper's role coming up on the Nov 5 call; the interviewer did not challenge it.
Witness said he may have said the payment should be resolved and was not overriding anyone; not challenged.
Who else should we speak with to understand these transactions?
I'd like to show you the Southampton Place partnership agreement, dated March 20, 2000.
Described the document's $25,000 contribution from the Fastow Family Foundation and asked whether it was the investment the witness had mentioned.
Here is LJM2's October 2000 report to its investors.
It lists returns of 193, 278, and 2,500 percent on the Raptor transactions, against the roughly 30 percent the Board was shown. Are those the figures?
Showed a handwritten note from Kopper addressed to 'Andy' referring to $10.5 million for the Chewco buyout, after first asking about the buyout.
Asked him to help reconcile his earlier statement that he stayed out of the buyout with the note's reference to $10.5 million.

tips: When a witness says 'I don't recall', which specific document or person in the record can you use to test that answer, and what exact question will you ask next?
For each key claim, how do you know it, did you see it yourself or hear it from someone, and how certain are you?
